narrative.recommendations_md:
All 12 recommendations follow the mandatory protocol: (1) E-IDs confirm the gap exists, (2) proxy searches are exhausted, (3) each maps to a named Zennify solution from the 12-solution catalog, (4) no investment amounts, ROI projections, or specific timelines are included per Hard Rule R6. Technology duplication check: 3 recommendations are platform activations on the confirmed 2023 Salesforce Sales Cloud org; 1 is a portal migration; 1 is conditional; 7 are greenfield.
: Digital Strategy & Vision Articulation Workshop [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
CACU scores 1.18 on (Digital Strategy & Vision) vs peer median 2.80, and 1.54 on (Governance & Risk Appetite) vs peer median 3.30 — the two largest category gaps in the assessment (−1.62 and −1.76 respectively). The primary driver is not operational absence but IC-010 inverse-TPRM positioning: as the trusted wholesale third-party for 533 member CUs, CACU deliberately keeps detailed public governance artifacts sparse for security reasons. However, the ABSENCE of a documented digital strategy creates two tangible risks: (1) the <2.5 connected cap suppresses 81 P3 capability scores — removing it restores P3 to ~3.4, closing the majority of CACU's peer gap in one move; (2) member CUs evaluating CACU as a technology partner have no publicly accessible transformation narrative to anchor their trust. The existing Salesforce Sales Cloud adoption (2023, E-NEW-SF-001) has not been articulated in any strategic roadmap.
[SOLUTION]
A Zennify-facilitated Digital Strategy Workshop produces: (a) a formal digital maturity roadmap anchored to CACU's 5 Strategic Objectives and existing technology investments; (b) a governance framework that can be selectively published to member CUs to demonstrate strategic intent without exposing internal controls; (c) a stakeholder-ready narrative framing the 2023 Salesforce adoption, Aptys joint-ownership, and Identifee IDA as components of a coherent digital transformation. The deliverable also triggers the connected cap reversal, restoring ~81 P3 capability scores. No new technology is required — this is a consulting engagement.
Implementation approach: 2-day onsite facilitation with C-suite (CEO Pritts, CSO Howle, CINO Coffey, CTO Eagen); structured around CACU's 5 SOs; output includes 12-month roadmap and governance charter
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: P3 +0.82 (connected cap reversal) | GRC Platform requires governance charter as prerequisite
: Financial Services Cloud — Upgrade Sales Cloud to FSC for Member-CU Lifecycle Management [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
 (Onboarding & Fulfillment) scores 1.74 vs peer median 3.10 (−1.36). Despite having Salesforce Sales Cloud since 2023, member-CU onboarding remains largely email/phone-driven. The sso.corpam.org portal provides access but not lifecycle orchestration — there is no KYC/CDD automation, no onboarding workflow, no compliance-aware digital onboarding specific to NCUA Part 704 wholesale membership requirements. (Compliance, Supervision & Surveillance) at 2.60 vs peer median 3.70 (−1.10) reflects the same gap: §748 ISP [E-131] and NCUA Part 704 [E-130] compliance is operationally sound but not systematically embedded in member-facing workflows.
⚡ Platform Note: CACU has Salesforce Sales Cloud (2023, E-NEW-SF-001). FSC is an upgrade path within the existing Salesforce org — no new vendor relationship required.
[SOLUTION]
Upgrade the existing Salesforce Sales Cloud org to Financial Services Cloud — a purpose-built CRM for financial services institutions with: (a) Part-704-aware member-CU onboarding workflows with built-in compliance checkpoints; (b) KYC/CDD automation aligned to NCUA regulatory requirements; (c) member-CU relationship lifecycle tracking (PCC tier, service utilization, engagement history); (d) compliance audit trail for §748 ISP obligations. This is an org-level upgrade, not a new deployment — the existing Salesforce environment, user accounts, and API integrations carry forward.
Implementation approach: Zennify FSC upgrade engagement; 6-9 months; leverages existing Sales Cloud org; integrates with NXTsoft OmniConnect [E-165] for data feeds
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Shield becomes applicable once FSC expands the PII surface | Agentforce can extend FSC case management into AI-triage
: Marketing Cloud — B2B Member Acquisition Automation for 440 Non-Participating CUs [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
 (Digital Marketing & Acquisition) scores 1.94 vs peer median 3.10 (−1.16). CACU's current outbound marketing infrastructure is limited to: LinkedIn presence (704 followers [E-059]), a static event calendar on corpam.org [E-052], and email blasts. There is no behavioral segmentation, no journey automation, and no digital acquisition funnel for the 440 non-participating member CUs that CEO Pritts identified as the primary PCC growth pool (SO-1). The existing Salesforce Sales Cloud org (E-NEW-SF-001) has no Marketing Cloud connected — the two systems are licensed separately.
[SOLUTION]
Connect Salesforce Marketing Cloud to the existing Salesforce org to deliver: (a) behavioral segmentation of the 533 member CUs by service utilization, PCC tier, and engagement frequency; (b) automated multi-touch journey campaigns targeting the 440 non-participating CUs with tailored RTP/FedNow adoption content; (c) AI-powered send-time optimization and A/B testing; (d) engagement attribution connecting marketing touchpoints to PCC tier upgrades. This leverages the existing Salesforce ecosystem without a new vendor relationship.
Implementation approach: Marketing Cloud connect to existing Sales Cloud org; 3-6 months; data integration via NXTsoft OmniData for segmentation signals
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Experience Cloud serves as the landing/portal destination for Marketing Cloud campaigns
: Service Cloud — Activate Omnichannel Member-CU Service Desk on Existing Salesforce Org [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
 (Omnichannel Servicing & Support) scores 2.05 vs peer median 3.20 (−1.15). The 533 member CUs today interact with CACU primarily through the SSO portal [E-217], telephone, and email. There is no unified case management system, no shared service ticket tracking, and no service-level dashboard for member CUs to monitor their requests. (Core Process Automation) at 2.54 vs peer median 3.60 (−1.06) reflects the absence of workflow automation: payment exception handling, wire inquiries, and compliance questions are manually routed across CACU's 5-track operational migration [IC-004].
⚡ Platform Note: CACU has Salesforce Sales Cloud (2023). Service Cloud = same Salesforce org, activated license. No new platform procurement.
[SOLUTION]
Activate Salesforce Service Cloud on the existing CACU org to deliver: (a) unified case management across all 533 member CUs with shared service-request visibility; (b) automated case routing by inquiry type (payment exceptions → operations; compliance questions → BSA team; technology issues → IT); (c) self-service case submission integrated with sso.corpam.org; (d) agent-facing unified desktop with full member-CU relationship context from the FSC org ( dependency). Service Cloud activation on an existing org takes weeks, not months.
Implementation approach: Service Cloud license activation + Zennify configuration; 4-6 months for full deployment; Case routing rules aligned to CACU's operational structure
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Agentforce extends Service Cloud with AI-triage | Experience Cloud provides the member-CU-facing self-service portal front-end
: CRM Analytics (Tableau) — Member-CU Self-Service Analytics Layer Above NXTsoft OmniLytics [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
 (Analytics & AI Enablement) scores 3.30 vs peer median 2.80 (+0.50) — CACU's strongest relative position. However, this strength is CACU-internal: NXTsoft OmniLytics produces quantitative analytics for CACU's own ALM, CECL, and risk functions. Member CUs do not have self-service access to analytics about their own account activity, payment volumes, or liquidity position. The gap is not in CACU's internal analytics but in EXTENDING analytics as a member-CU-facing product, which is the next competitive differentiation layer.
[SOLUTION]
Deploy Salesforce CRM Analytics (Tableau) as a member-CU-facing analytics product connected to NXTsoft OmniLytics data feeds — NOT replacing OmniLytics, but providing: (a) member-CU dashboards for their own payment volumes, liquidity ratios, and CECL position accessible via the Experience Cloud portal; (b) Salesforce-embedded analytics within the FSC org for CACU relationship managers; (c) predictive analytics for member-CU PCC upgrade likelihood (input to Marketing Cloud targeting). CRM Analytics licenses into the existing Salesforce org.
Implementation approach: CRM Analytics + Tableau license activation; data connector to NXTsoft OmniData/OmniLytics; 4-6 months; embedded in Experience Cloud portal
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Data Cloud feeds CRM Analytics with unified data | Experience Cloud is the delivery portal
: Agentforce — Extend Identifee IDA AI Model Into Sales and Service Domains [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
CACU launched Identifee IDA in September 2024 [E-128] — the first corporate CU with a production AI chatbot, scoped specifically to Nacha Operating Rules & Guidelines. This is a proven AI deployment that demonstrates CACU's ability to execute GenAI. However, IDA's scope is intentionally narrow: it answers Nacha compliance questions. The AI capability exists but is NOT deployed for: (a) member-CU sales prospecting and PCC tier analysis; (b) service ticket triage within the Salesforce org; (c) operations queue management (payment exceptions, wire queries). at 2.54 vs peer median 3.60 reflects this automation gap.
⚡ Platform Note: Identifee IDA is in production (Sept 2024) — CACU's first corporate-CU GenAI/RAG chatbot. Agentforce extends IDA into new domains on the existing Salesforce org. NOT duplicating IDA.
[SOLUTION]
Deploy Salesforce Agentforce agents within the existing CACU Salesforce org to: (a) a Sales Agent that surfaces non-participating member CU engagement signals and suggests outreach actions to CACU relationship managers; (b) a Service Agent that auto-triages incoming cases in Service Cloud by inquiry type, routing and drafting initial responses; (c) an Operations Agent that monitors payment exception queues and surfaces resolution suggestions. These agents are ADDITIVE to Identifee IDA — they operate in different domains (Nacha compliance vs CRM/service vs operations) and would be positioned to member CUs as 'CACU's AI ecosystem expanding beyond payments.'
Implementation approach: Agentforce configuration on existing Salesforce org; requires Service Cloud and FSC as prerequisites; 6-9 months; Zennify AI practice leads
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Extends Service Cloud value | Enhances FSC relationship management
: Experience Cloud — Modernize sso.corpam.org Member Portal [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
The existing sso.corpam.org portal [E-217] serves as the primary self-service interface for 533 member credit unions — providing SSO access to CACU's payment, imaging, and banking services. However, it is a custom-built portal without: (a) CRM data integration (member-CU interactions are not unified with Salesforce); (b) self-service case submission (Service Cloud dependency, ); (c) personalized content delivery based on member-CU service utilization tier; (d) embedded analytics access (CRM Analytics dependency, ). (Personalization) at 2.68 vs peer median 2.80 (−0.12) would move materially once the portal delivers personalized content by PCC tier.
⚡ Platform Note: sso.corpam.org is a custom SSO portal confirmed in production [E-217]. This is a MODERNIZATION/MIGRATION, not a greenfield build. Existing portal functionality migrates to Experience Cloud.
[SOLUTION]
Migrate sso.corpam.org to Salesforce Experience Cloud — not a rebuild from scratch, but a platform migration that: (a) preserves all existing SSO and service-access functionality; (b) connects the portal natively to the Salesforce CRM org (FSC, Service Cloud, Agentforce); (c) enables personalized landing pages by member-CU PCC tier, service utilization, and onboarding stage; (d) serves as the front-end for self-service case submission, analytics dashboards, and AI-assisted guidance. The Kentico CMS content can be migrated or federated into Experience Cloud.
Implementation approach: Experience Cloud site build + SSO migration; 4-8 months; Zennify Experience Cloud practice; preserves member-CU user accounts and service access patterns
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Portal front-end for Service Cloud, CRM Analytics, Agentforce | Marketing Cloud campaigns land on personalized portal pages
: Slack — Unified Internal Collaboration for 5-Track Migration Coordination [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
 (Culture & Change Enablement) scores 1.17 vs peer median 2.40 (−1.23). CACU is simultaneously managing 5 operational migration tracks per IC-004: (1) Aptys payments migration (Dec 2024), (2) VSoft core upgrade, (3) Identifee IDA expansion, (4) FedNow/RTP ecosystem growth, (5) NXTsoft OmniConnect integration layer. With ~40-50 employees, coordinating these tracks across a small team without a dedicated collaboration platform creates change-management risk. The current Microsoft Azure stack [E-178] suggests email and potentially MS Teams, but no collaboration tool specifically tuned for project-based Salesforce/fintech delivery is confirmed.
[SOLUTION]
Deploy Slack as CACU's primary internal collaboration and workflow platform, with: (a) Salesforce-native integration connecting CRM cases, Agentforce alerts, and CRM Analytics notifications directly to Slack channels; (b) project channels per migration track (Aptys, VSoft, FedNow, IDA-Agentforce, Experience Cloud); (c) automated Salesforce workflow notifications (case updates, PCC tier changes, payment alerts) surfaced in Slack; (d) searchable institutional knowledge base for compliance Q&A (complementary to member-facing IDA). The Salesforce-Slack integration is built-in to all Salesforce tiers.
Implementation approach: Slack workspace setup + Salesforce integration; 1-2 months; Zennify configuration; no complex data migration
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Slack provides the operational communication layer for all T1-T3 Salesforce activations
: Salesforce Shield — §748 ISP Encryption Overlay on Expanded Salesforce Org [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
CACU already demonstrates strong cybersecurity posture: 89% NIST CSF (87/98 subcategories) [E-160], ISE Core Plus [E-131], §748 ISP compliance. (Cybersecurity) at 3.60 is the strongest category, +0.20 vs peer median. However, as the Salesforce org expands to hold member-CU PII (FSC:, Service Cloud case data:, Marketing Cloud contact records: ), the §748 ISP encryption obligations apply to Salesforce data at rest. Current encryption controls (Imperva WAF, Azure DRaaS encryption) do NOT cover Salesforce field-level data. Shield adds: (a) Platform Encryption for Salesforce fields containing PII; (b) Event Monitoring for compliance audit trail; (c) Field Audit Trail for §748 data retention.
[SOLUTION]
Deploy Salesforce Shield — Platform Encryption + Event Monitoring — on the expanded CACU Salesforce org after FSC and Service Cloud are operational ( + ). Shield is a Salesforce add-on that does not require infrastructure changes. It extends CACU's existing §748 ISP [E-131] data protection controls into the Salesforce platform layer, ensuring that member-CU PII in CRM records is encrypted at rest with CACU-managed keys.
Implementation approach: Shield license activation; Zennify security practice configuration; 2-3 months; prerequisite: FSC + Service Cloud
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Protects score from deteriorating as PII surface expands
: GRC Platform — Automate Audit Finding Closure and Governance Workflow [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
 (Governance & Risk Appetite) at 1.54 vs peer median 3.30 (−1.76) is the #1 priority gap. Despite a CLEAN regulatory record (no NCUA enforcement, consent orders, LUAs, or CMPs), CACU's governance infrastructure relies on a manual 4-firm audit structure (Doeren Mayhew + CRI + Forvis Mazars + ePay Advisors [E-160]) with no dedicated GRC platform for systematic finding closure, remediation tracking, or risk appetite quantification. (Business Resilience & Third-Party Management) at 2.60 vs peer median 3.40 (−0.80) reflects the same infrastructure gap: CACU IS the third-party risk subject for 533 member CUs but lacks a formal TPRM platform to manage its own vendor risk and demonstrate due diligence beyond the annual DD packet [E-160].
[SOLUTION]
Deploy a Salesforce-native GRC Platform within the existing CACU Salesforce org to: (a) convert audit findings from all 4 firms into tracked, owner-assigned GRC cases with closure deadlines; (b) automate risk appetite threshold monitoring and board-reportable risk registers; (c) manage CACU's own vendor/TPRM inventory (Aptys, NXTsoft, VSoft, Pidgin, ThreatAdvice, etc.) with annual review workflows; (d) produce board-ready governance dashboards for the quarterly board reporting cycle. Deployed on the existing Salesforce org — no separate GRC system required.
Implementation approach: Salesforce GRC (Risk Management) configuration; Zennify compliance practice; 4-6 months; integrates with existing Salesforce org
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Primary enabler of ≥2.5 → unlocks connected cap reversal on 81 P3 subcaps (combined with )
: Data Cloud — Unified Member-CU CDP Above NXTsoft + Aptys + VSoft [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
CACU's data infrastructure is operationally strong: VSoft Wings/Vantage core [E-164], NXTsoft OmniConnect/OmniData/OmniLytics [E-165], Aptys Solutions [E-108]. (Data Management & Governance) at 3.37 is +0.47 above peer median. However, the data is siloed across three operational systems: VSoft (core banking/account data), Aptys (payment transaction data), and NXTsoft (API events and analytics). There is no unified member-CU identity layer that connects a member CU's core account activity, payment behavior, and service engagement history into a single profile. (Personalization) at 2.68 is constrained by this fragmentation — you cannot personalize without a unified 360-degree member-CU profile.
[SOLUTION]
Deploy Salesforce Data Cloud as a CDP overlay connecting NXTsoft OmniData, Aptys payment data, and VSoft account data — NOT replacing any existing system, but creating a unified member-CU identity resolution layer that: (a) resolves the same credit union's identity across all three data systems using the VSoft Vantage universal CIF as the primary identity anchor; (b) surfaces real-time member-CU payment activity and liquidity signals into the Salesforce FSC org; (c) activates behavioral segments for Marketing Cloud campaigns without manual data extraction; (d) provides the data foundation for Agentforce agents to surface context-aware recommendations.
Implementation approach: Data Cloud provisioning + data connectors to NXTsoft/VSoft/Aptys APIs; 6-9 months; requires NXTsoft OmniConnect APIs for data ingestion (existing integration layer)
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Feeds CRM Analytics with unified data | Enables Marketing Cloud real-time segmentation | Context layer for Agentforce
: MuleSoft Anypoint — Cross-Vendor Orchestration Above NXTsoft OmniConnect [ZENNIFY]
[ROOT CAUSE]
CACU is executing 5 concurrent technology migrations per IC-004: Aptys payments (Dec 2024), VSoft core upgrade, Identifee IDA, FedNow/RTP ecosystem expansion, and NXTsoft integration layer changes. Each migration introduces new API connections; NXTsoft OmniConnect [E-165] manages current point-to-point APIs but lacks enterprise-grade workflow orchestration for MULTI-SYSTEM processes. (Core Process Automation) at 2.54 vs peer median 3.60 (−1.06) reflects the absence of cross-system workflow automation: a payment exception involves VSoft (core), Aptys (payment), NXTsoft (event notification), and the Salesforce org (case creation, ) — four systems that today require manual hand-offs between each step.
⚡ Platform Note: NXTsoft OmniConnect is confirmed for current API integration [E-165]. MuleSoft operates at a higher orchestration layer — managing multi-system workflows, NOT replacing OmniConnect point-to-point integrations.
[SOLUTION]
Deploy MuleSoft Anypoint as the enterprise integration and orchestration layer ABOVE NXTsoft OmniConnect, handling: (a) multi-system orchestration for payment exception workflows (VSoft → Aptys → NXTsoft → Salesforce Service Cloud); (b) ISO 20022 message transformation for FedNow/RTP rails [E-114]; (c) standardized API gateway for the 5-track migration — each new system connects to MuleSoft once, not to every other system (n-to-1 vs n-to-n); (d) real-time data streaming to Data Cloud from VSoft and Aptys. OmniConnect continues handling its existing CACU↔member-CU API calls — MuleSoft operates at the CACU-internal orchestration layer.
Implementation approach: MuleSoft Anypoint Platform; Zennify integration practice; 6-12 months for full orchestration layer; prioritize payment exception workflow in month 1-3
[EXPECTED OUTCOMES]
connected unlocks: Enables Data Cloud real-time data streaming | Provides integration backbone for Service Cloud payment exception workflows
narrative.roadmap_md: The transformation roadmap organizes the 12 recommendations into four sequential phases, each building on the prior. Phases are milestone-anchored, not date-anchored. No investment amounts, cost estimates, or specific timelines appear in this section (Hard Rule R6). The critical insight: CACU already owns Salesforce Sales Cloud (2023, [E-NEW-SF-001]) — Phases 2, 3, and 4 are platform activations on an existing org, not new vendor relationships.
